title: Themeable Design System & Performance Overhaul
description: I built a themeable component library from scratch and lifted Lighthouse scores from roughly 35 to 90 through profiling and bundle optimization.

seo.title: Themeable Design System & Performance Overhaul — Case Study
seo.description: How I built a themeable component library and lifted Lighthouse scores from roughly 35 to 90 through profiling and bundle optimization.

sections.title: No design language, and a Lighthouse score to match.

items.src: The application had no consistent design language. Components were built ad hoc for whatever feature needed them, with no shared theming or accessibility baseline. Performance suffered along with it: Lighthouse scores sat around 35, which meant slow load times and a worse ranking signal on top of the poor user experience.

src: No shared component library, so every feature reinvented its own UI.
No theming layer, making visual consistency and dark mode impossible.
Lighthouse scores around 35 on key pages, well below a usable baseline.

sections.title: Build the system, then profile the runtime.

items.src: I designed and built a reusable, themeable component library with Emotion, so every feature team pulled from the same set of primitives instead of writing their own. With that in place, I used Chrome DevTools to profile the bundle and runtime, then applied code splitting, lazy loading, and tree shaking wherever the profiler pointed.

src.title: Shared primitives over per-feature components
src.desc: Every new UI element started from the shared library instead of a fresh implementation, which is what made the theming layer possible in the first place.

src.title: Profile before optimizing
src.desc: Rather than guessing at slow paths, I used Chrome DevTools to find the actual bottlenecks first, then targeted code splitting and lazy loading at those specific routes.

items.src: Retrofitting a theme layer onto existing screens

Existing screens had hardcoded styles baked in throughout, with no theming abstraction to hook into. I introduced Emotion's theming provider incrementally, migrating one screen at a time so the app stayed shippable throughout the rollout.

A Lighthouse score of 35 doesn't say which part of the app is the problem. I used Chrome DevTools' performance and coverage panels to isolate unused JavaScript and render-blocking resources before touching any code.

src.label: Lighthouse score after profiling and optimization
Shared component library adopted across the team
Visual regressions during the theme migration

items.src: A design system is a performance decision, not just a visual one.

Building the shared component library first made the performance work easier, not harder: fixing a render pattern once in the library fixed it everywhere the library was used. Design consistency and runtime performance turned out to be the same problem, approached from two angles.
